title: Detailed depiction gives way to a fading tile field

source.creator: John Knopf (@johnknopf), original poster; shared by Phil Trubey (@PTrubey)
source.title: All the Way Here

motion.summary: A readable silhouetted human scene is replaced by a coarse field of warm and dark squares. The tile field holds across a lyric, then darkens before the next figurative scene appears.
phases: A detailed, text-textured human silhouette provides an emotional anchor.
The image changes to a coarse square field with no comparably clear figure.
The abstract field holds while the lyric remains separate.
The squares fade toward near-black before a new depiction enters.
motion.transferablePrinciple: After a concrete emotional image, deliberately remove representational detail and let a simpler visual field carry uncertainty or a pause.
variations: Reduce a new crowded scene to a sparse arrangement of a few meaningful shapes.
After a detailed memory, hold an original field of fragments and let them dim before the next scene.
Use a brief shift in visual density between two otherwise complex chapters.
cautions: The inspected frames show replacement by tiles; they do not prove that individual image pixels continuously morph into the grid.
Do not reproduce the exact tile arrangement, palette or preceding figure.
A quiet field needs a short intentional role; repeated or long abstract holds can feel like filler.
Keep the lyric more readable than the sampled source at small sizes.

quality.reviewer: agent visual inspection of decoded frame sequence
strengths: A strong change in visual detail distinguishes introspection from the surrounding depictions.
The dimming field creates space before the next recognizable scene.
limitations: The coarse grid is visually static in the sampled middle frames; the idea is contrast and fading, not elaborate motion.
The dark source and small subtitle scale limit phone readability.
quality.userPreferenceScope: Source video only. Shane noted cool ideas in the video; this individual excerpt has not been approved. No numerical craft or timing score assigned.
